name: Urartian
confidence_why: Diakonoff 1971, Wilhelm 2004 and Khachikyan 2010 all infer from cuneiform spellings that Urartian stress fell on the penultimate syllable in most words, with final stress on certain nouns in -a/-ə and shifts before some suffixes, and all three hedge the claim, so the record stays undetermined with penult as the only candidate and no source against it.

new_statements.quote: В У.я., вероятно, было довольно сильное экспираторное ударение на предпоследнем слоге. На это указывает нейтрализация конечных i, e, a, ср. al-su-i-še ‛величие’ при al-su-i-ši-i-ni ‛величием’, ši-ú-li-i-e ‛<тот, кто> унесет’ при ši-ú-li-a-li ‛<тот, кто> унесет-их’. Конечный гласный -а в локативном показателе (см. 2.4.0.) и в многочисленных теонимах, антропонимах и нарицательных именах, обозначающих лиц, предположительно был ударным или несущим контурный тон (ср. теоним Aya, антропоним Ruca, существительное cila ‛жена’). Контурный тон могли нести также стяженные гласные и дифтонги.
new_statements.translation: In Urartian there was probably a fairly strong expiratory stress on the penultimate syllable. This is indicated by the neutralization of final i, e, a, cf. al-su-i-še 'greatness' beside al-su-i-ši-i-ni 'by greatness', ši-ú-li-i-e '<he who> will carry off' beside ši-ú-li-a-li '<he who> will carry-them-off'. The final vowel -a in the locative marker (see 2.4.0.) and in numerous theonyms, anthroponyms and common nouns denoting persons was presumably stressed or bore a contour tone (cf. the theonym Aya, the anthroponym Ruca, the noun cila 'wife'). Contracted vowels and diphthongs may also have borne a contour tone.

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Urartian (catalog-all-2026-09-12) has an empty rule and there are no existing stress statements, so this is the first placement statement held by the project: penultimate expiratory stress (hedged), with final-stress/contour-tone exceptions on words ending in -a. Nothing to agree with or contradict.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Probably a fairly strong expiratory (dynamic) stress on the penultimate syllable, inferred from the orthographic neutralization of word-final i/e/a (unstressed final vowels reduce). Vowel length is not phonemic but prosodic: stressed syllables and syllables with contour tone were longer; the shortest syllable is a final open syllable without contour tone (p. 154, 2.1.4). Plene writing is taken as possibly marking tone rather than length.
new_statements.exceptions: Word-final -a in the locative marker and in many theonyms, anthroponyms and nouns for persons (Aya, Ruca, cila 'wife') was presumably stressed or carried a contour tone, i.e. final stress in those forms; the same inference is repeated in fn. 3 p. 162 (a case formant in final -a 'was stressed') and on p. 164 ('final -a was stressed or bore a contour tone'). Contracted vowels and diphthongs may have borne contour tone. All statements are hedged ('вероятно', 'предположительно') as reconstructions from cuneiform spelling.
new_statements.identity_note: Urartian is an extinct language attested in cuneiform inscriptions (9th-6th c. BCE); no dialect is distinguished. Khachikyan's stress statement is a philological reconstruction from the neutralization of final vowels and from plene writing, not a description of a spoken variety.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.recode_to: no reclassification required. Note for a reviewer: three independent authorities (Diakonoff 1971 'anscheinend.. in den meisten Fällen', Wilhelm 2004 'seems.. at least in certain cases, defined by unknown conditions', Khachikyan 2010 'вероятно.. довольно сильное экспираторное ударение на предпоследнем слоге') all name the penult and none names any other default; if catalog policy codes a unanimously reported but hedged position, the alternative coding would be penult (tentative, philologically inferred) with morphologically/lexically listed final-stress exceptions (-ə nouns per Diakonoff; locative -a and person names per Khachikyan). Under the current policy (hedged statements with unknown conditioning = not determinable, as ruled 2026-09-12) the record stands.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every deciding sentence is verbatim at the stated line ranges in the scanned files we hold (Diakonoff 1971 p.58 sec.9 l.3524-3535, p.37 h) l.2147-2164, fn.30 l.2197-2213; Wilhelm CEWAL 2004 p.123 l.10464-10471; 2008 p.109 snippet identical). (2) Deciding sources are grammar sketches (1971 comparative sketch, 2004 encyclopedia chapter) but they are the standard authorities for an extinct cuneiform language whose accent is only philologically inferable; no instrumental or dedicated prosody study can exist. tone.quote: There is a system of five (or six) vowels, i e a (o?) u, and word-final ə (< e, i). Length distinction was probably phonemic. The extent of consonantal clusters in initial, medial, and final position is not certain. Accent appears to have been on the penult syllable. Assimilation and contraction are widely found: ereli-ne-lə > erelelə “kings.”
